geometry_edits.rationale: Shift the cantilever later so the lower edge can remain grounded near the access side while preserving the dominant bent mass.
Transform the overly abstract bend into a section-aware profile that can better support the neighborhood-living program and produce a clearer roof/section reading.
Use a folded section family to keep the dominant gesture continuous while giving the mass a more inhabitable sectional profile.
Maintain the long-axis bar logic so the primary mass remains a clear anchor.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the carved ground response with the verified access side so the frontage reads as a public threshold instead of a generic subtraction.
Enlarge the ground void so it becomes a legible public court/entry figure rather than a minor notch.
Increase the carve depth to strengthen the spatial consequence of the access-edge opening.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent bar with a stepped/cantilevered upper mass, and it is legible across all four views rather than collapsing into a single-view trick. The silhouette is resolved and not merely repetitive stair-step massing. However, the ground response is weak: the blue frontage edge is not answered by a clear public void, notch, or entry seam, so the street relationship remains semantically underdeveloped for neighborhood living. The parcel is broadly respected and the mass stays within it, but the open-space figure is too small and too internalized to fully satisfy the active-edge brief. Programmatically it can plausibly support a compact neighborhood mixed-use/residential bar, but the section still feels more like an abstract folded object than a building with a strong public ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a taller tower reference; the candidate is much lower and more compact, so only the sectional stepping logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked, capacity-aware massing with a legible profile shift can support mixed-use without becoming purely ornamental.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is not a tower; avoid importing the tall-object typology or overemphasizing verticality.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A slender, slightly torqued vertical mass can express hierarchy and urban presence while keeping a coherent primary volume.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a small café/restaurant object; the candidate needs a more substantial mixed-use residential reading and stronger courtyard/void logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple active-ground commercial bar with a clear canopy/threshold is a useful precedent for street-facing legibility.

warnings: Public threshold along the verified access edge is insufficiently articulated.
Void/court logic is present only as a small cut and does not read as a meaningful usable open space.
Upper stepping/cantilever is coherent, but the ground program relation needs strengthening.
